ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, two small balls A and B, both of mass m, are connected by a thin string. Small ball A is connected to a light spring, and the other end of the spring is fixed on a vertical wall. Small ball A is connected to the ceiling by a thin string. At the beginning, both small balls are at rest. At this time, the angle between the thin string and the horizontal direction is $\theta=45^{\circ}$, the spring is horizontal, and the acceleration due to gravity is g. Now the thin string is suddenly cut. At the instant the string is cut, what is the magnitude of the acceleration of small ball A?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is a vertical wall, and the top is a horizontal ceiling; small ball A is located at the right end of the spring, and the spring is horizontally connected to the left wall; A is also connected to the ceiling through a thin string slanting upward to the right, and the angle between this thin string and the horizontal direction is labeled θ; small ball B is directly below A, and A and B are connected by a vertical thin string. Then reason: when initially at rest, let the tension in the oblique thin string on the ceiling be T, the magnitude of the horizontal pulling force exerted by the spring on A be F, and the tension in the thin string between A and B be T0. For the equilibrium of B: T0=mg. For the equilibrium of A: in the vertical direction there is T sinθ = mg + T0 = 2mg; in the horizontal direction there is F = T cosθ. Therefore F = 2mg cotθ. In the problem θ=45°, so F=2mg. At the instant the ceiling thin string is cut, the deformation of the spring has no time to change, so the horizontal force exerted by the spring on A is still 2mg, directed to the left; A is still acted on by gravity mg, and the thin string between A and B keeps a vertical constraint. Let the tension in the thin string between A and B at the instant of cutting be T1, and take vertically downward as positive. Then the vertical equation for A is m a_Ay = mg + T1, and the vertical equation for B is m a_By = mg - T1. Since the thin string between A and B is instantaneously vertical and inextensible, and the initial velocities of the two balls are zero, the accelerations along the string direction are the same, that is, a_Ay=a_By. Thus mg+T1 = mg-T1, giving T1=0, so a_Ay=g, directed downward. In the horizontal direction, A is acted on only by the spring force, so a_Ax=F/m=2g, directed to the left. Therefore the magnitude of the acceleration of A is sqrt((2g)^2+g^2)=sqrt(5)g.
